Theme

Tools, fasteners & household repair · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

strike verb

hit

also knock, hit, beat, be beaten, get a thrashing, wallop, get walloped, get a whipping, whack

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.5.142: ad pulsandōs verberandōsque hominēs (Lewis & Short)

pulsō, pulsāre

verb, first conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

strike, knock

Of knocking at a door (ōstium pulsāre) and of hitting people.

Other words

  • feriō, ferīre — strike, hit (with a blow)

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Quint. 2.8.13: pugnō ferīre vel calce (Lewis & Short); Hor. C. 1.1.36: sublīmī feriam sīdera vertice · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    No perfect: percussī serves (Lewis & Short, after Varro).

  • percutiō, percutere, percussī, percussum — strike, hit

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Quint. 1.9.5: paedagōgum ejus percussit; Cic. de Or. 2.279: cum Catō percussus esset ab eō, quī arcam ferēbat (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • verberō, verberāre, verberāvī, verberātum — beat, thrash

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 562: nōn puduisse verberāre hominem senem · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • vāpulō, vāpulāre, vāpulāvī — be beaten, get a thrashing

    verb, first conjugation, intransitive: active in form, passive in sense · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 213: ego vāpulandō, ille verberandō; Traupman 403, 406 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (vōx plērumque cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; in ōrātiōne solūtā rārior)

    The partner of verberō: verberat, he beats; vāpulat, he gets beaten.

  • caedō, caedere, cecīdī, caesum — beat, strike (with fists or clubs)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short; Traupman 278 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • īcō, īcere, īcī, ictum — hit, strike

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 328 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • percolopō, percolopāre — box someone’s ears, wallop

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Petr. 44.5: lārvās sīc istōs percolopābant (Lewis & Short); Traupman 403, 406 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Petr.)

    A word of Petronius’s freedmen; found only there.

Examples

  • ut Cratēs, cum indoctum puerum vīdisset, paedagōgum ejus percussit

    as Crates, when he saw an ignorant boy, struck the boy’s tutorQuint. 1.9.5

  • Nōlī frātrem pulsāre!

    Don’t hit your brother!composed

  • Ego vāpulandō, ille verberandō, ūsque ambō dēfessī sumus.

    I with being beaten, he with beating, we’re both worn out.Ter. Ad. 213

  • vāpulāre

    to get walloped, get a beatingTraupman 403

See also hammer, hit.
